event_description: State of emergency for the wildfires, declared Monday, May 8, 2000 ('The state is a tinderbox'), while the Cerro Grande fire burned at Los Alamos and a fire near Ruidoso forced hundreds to flee (Associated Press report of May 9, 2000)

State disaster declared for Eddy, Mora, San Miguel and Bernalillo counties, making them eligible for state disaster assistance after the severe storms and flooding of April 2004 (dated report of May 4, 2004; the signing day is not given)
State of disaster in eight counties for widespread flooding from heavy rain and thunderstorms
State disaster area declared in Clovis after the tornado of March 23, 2007
Lincoln and Otero counties declared disaster areas for the flooding of July 27, 2008
Disaster declared for flood damage from heavy rains in Socorro, Mora and McKinley counties, part of the Navajo Nation, Farmington and the Pueblo of Acoma
State of emergency for natural gas outages caused by extreme cold
Disaster declared in Sandoval County due to flooding
Emergency declared throughout New Mexico due to enhanced flood potential caused by severe wildfires
Emergency declared throughout New Mexico due to the severe storms and flooding across the state in July
State of disaster declared statewide due to flooding from record rain
Emergency declaration for flooding from recent heavy rains, providing emergency aid and authorizing the National Guard
Emergency declared throughout New Mexico due to flooding from Hurricane Odile
